title: Math Banking Class 10 ICSE Test
description: Math Banking Class 10 ICSE Test simple and complex interest
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A vendor supplying fresh vegetables for Hari Tokri deposits ₹500 per month in a recurring deposit account for 2 years. If the rate of interest is 8% p.a., find the total interest earned by the vendor.
questions.explanation:
Given, Monthly installment (P) = ₹500, Time (n) = 2 years = 24 months, Rate (r) = 8% p.a.
The formula for interest is I = P \times \frac{n(n+1)}{2 \times 12} \times \frac{r}{100}.
I = 500 \times \frac{24 \times 25}{24} \times \frac{8}{100}
I = 5 \times 25 \times 8 = 1000.
The total interest earned is ₹1,000.

questions.question: A developer at Launch Your Concept opened a recurring deposit account with a Nationalised Bank for a period of 2 years. If the bank pays interest at the rate of 6% per annum and the monthly installment is ₹1,000, find the maturity value of the account.
questions.explanation:
Given, P = ₹1,000, n = 24 months, r = 6% p.a.
First, calculate the interest: I = 1000 \times \frac{24 \times 25}{24} \times \frac{6}{100} = 10 \times 25 \times 6 = 1500.
Total principal deposited = 1000 \times 24 = ₹24,000.
Maturity Value (MV) = Total Principal + Interest = 24000 + 1500 = ₹25,500.

questions.question: An educational consultant managing the OMD Leads platform gets ₹16,176 on maturity of his recurring deposit account. If the rate of interest is 8% p.a. and the total period is 3 years, find his monthly installment.
questions.explanation:
Let the monthly installment be P. n = 3 years = 36 months, r = 8%, MV = ₹16,176.
Interest I = P \times \frac{36 \times 37}{24} \times \frac{8}{100} = P \times \frac{3 \times 37}{2} \times 0.08 = P \times 111 \times 0.04 = 4.
Maturity Value = (P \times 36) + I.
16176 = 36P + 4.44P = 40.44P.
P = \frac{16176}{40.44} = 400.
The monthly installment is ₹400.

questions.question: A merchant selling plywood on Ply Dekho has a recurring deposit account for 3 years at a monthly installment of ₹200. If he gets ₹8,088 at the time of maturity, find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.explanation:
Given, P = ₹200, n = 36 months, MV = ₹8,088. Let the rate be r%.
Total amount deposited = 200 \times 36 = ₹7,200.
Interest earned (I) = MV - Total Deposited = 8088 - 7200 = ₹888.
Using the formula: I = P \times \frac{n(n+1)}{24} \times \frac{r}{100}.
888 = 200 \times \frac{36 \times 37}{24} \times \frac{r}{100}.
888 = 2 \times 55.5 \times r = 111r.
r = \frac{888}{111} = 8\%.
The rate of interest is 8% p.a.

questions.question: A man has a recurring deposit account in a bank for ₹300 per month. If the rate of interest is 12% p.a. and he gets ₹8,100 on maturity, find the total time (in months) for which the account was held.
questions.explanation:
Given, P = ₹300, r = 12%, MV = ₹8,100. Let the time be n months.
Interest I = 300 \times \frac{n(n+1)}{24} \times \frac{12}{100} = 3 \times \frac{n^2 + n}{2} = 1.5n^2 + 1.5n.
Maturity Value = (300 \times n) + I.
8100 = 300n + 1.5n^2 + 1.5n.
1.5n^2 + 301.5n - 8100 = 0.
Dividing the entire equation by 1.5 gives: n^2 + 201n - 5400 = 0.
Factorizing: n^2 + 225n - 24n - 5400 = 0.
n(n + 225) - 24(n + 225) = 0 \implies (n - 24)(n + 225) = 0.
Since time cannot be negative, n = 24 months.

questions.question: Rekha opened a Recurring Deposit account and deposited ₹400 per month. If the rate of interest is 10% p.a. and the maturity value is ₹16,620, find the time of the investment in years.
questions.explanation:
Given, P = ₹400, r = 10%, MV = ₹16,620. Let time be n months.
Interest I = 400 \times \frac{n(n+1)}{24} \times \frac{10}{100} = \frac{40(n^2 + n)}{24} = \frac{5n^2 + 5n}{3}.
MV = (400 \times n) + I.
16620 = 400n + \frac{5n^2 + 5n}{3}.
Multiplying by 3: 49860 = 1200n + 5n^2 + 5n.
5n^2 + 1205n - 49860 = 0.
Divide by 5: n^2 + 241n - 9972 = 0.
Factorizing: n^2 + 277n - 36n - 9972 = 0 \implies (n - 36)(n + 277) = 0.
So, n = 36 months, which is equal to \frac{36}{12} = 3 years.

questions.question: Aman deposits ₹500 per month for 2 years at 8% p.a. in an RD account. Baman deposits ₹400 per month for 2.5 years at the same rate. Find the difference in their maturity values.
The maturity value of a recurring deposit account is ₹15,900 and the total interest earned is ₹1,500. Find the monthly installment and the rate of interest if the period is 2 years.
questions.explanation:
Given, MV = ₹15,900, I = ₹1,500, n = 24 months.
We know, MV = (P \times n) + I.
15900 = 24P + 1500.
24P = 14400 \implies P = \frac{14400}{24} = ₹600.
Now, substitute P in the interest formula:
1500 = 600 \times \frac{24 \times 25}{24} \times \frac{r}{100}.
1500 = 6 \times 25 \times r.
150r = 1500 \implies r = 10\%.
The monthly installment is ₹600 and the rate is 10%.

questions.question: Mohan has a recurring deposit account in a bank for 2 years at 6% p.a. simple interest. If he gets ₹1,200 as interest at the time of maturity, find his total maturity value.
questions.explanation:
Given, I = ₹1,200, n = 24 months, r = 6%.
1200 = P \times \frac{24 \times 25}{24} \times \frac{6}{100}.
1200 = P \times 25 \times 0.06.
1200 = 1.5P \implies P = \frac{1200}{1.5} = ₹800.
Total Principal Deposited = 800 \times 24 = ₹19,200.
Maturity Value = Principal + Interest = 19200 + 1200 = ₹20,400.

questions.question: David opened a Recurring Deposit Account in a bank and deposited ₹300 per month for two years. If he received ₹7,725 at the time of maturity, find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.explanation:
Given, P = ₹300, n = 24 months, MV = ₹7,725.
Total principal deposited = 300 \times 24 = ₹7,200.
Interest (I) = MV - Principal = 7725 - 7200 = ₹525.
Using the interest formula:
525 = 300 \times \frac{24 \times 25}{24} \times \frac{r}{100}.
525 = 3 \times 25 \times r = 75r.
r = \frac{525}{75} = 7\%.
The rate of interest is 7% per annum.
